To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

long-term electromagnetic field treatment can provide general memory benefit to very old mice, as well to young mice, and that it can reverse very advanced β-amyloid neuropathology in old mice without brain hyperthermic effects.
daily EMF exposure for several months can provide general cognitive benefits and reversal of advanced A β neuropathology in old Alzheimer's transgenic mice, without brain heating.

daily electromagnetic field exposure for 6+ months provides selected cognitive benefit to normal and Alzheimer's transgenic mice, while also providing protection against and reversal of brain β-β amyloid (Aβ aggregation/deposition, the hallmark neuropathology of Alzheimer's disease (AD) (see Fig. 1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of long-term (months) exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMF) on brain physiology and behavior in mice.
the impact of electromagnetic field exposure on the central nervous system.
the impact of electromagnetic fields (EMF) on the brain, particularly the impact of pulsed EMF on the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of these studies demonstrate that long-term exposure to pulsed electromagnetic fields can provide cognitive benefits to normal and Alzheimer's transgenic mice.
EMF exposure can be beneficial to the brain, and that this benefit is not mediated by hyperthermia.
long-term EMFs are effective in reversing advanced Alzheimer's pathology and in improving cognition in aged Alzheimer's mice, but that the mechanism of action is not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

long-term EMFs (1) can reverse advanced Aβ neuropathy in very old Tg mouse brains, (2) provide cognitive benefits to both Tg and non-Tg mouse brains, and (3) have no significant impact on brain temperature.
EMF treatment is neuroprotective in the brain, and that the neuroprotection occurs through multiple mechanisms.

daily exposure to EMF over a 6+ month period provides cognitive benefit to both normal and Alzheimer's mice and, for the Tg mice, involves suppression of Aβ aggregation/depositon, brain mitochondrial enhancement, and reduction in brain blood flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long-term EMFs can provide cognitive benefit in normal and AD mice, as well in normal humans, without brain hyperthermic effects.
EMF treatment is a noninvasive, nonpharmacological approach that can reverse or suppress Alzheimer's neuropathology and provide cognitive benefit to normal and Alzheimer's mice.
long-term EMFs can be beneficial in Alzheimer's mice and humans, but the mechanisms by which EMFs provide these benefits are not fully understood.
